attempts.label: DANDI:000946
attempts.paper_title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Modulates Feedforward and Feedback Cortico-Thalamo-Cortical Pathways by Selectively Activating Excitatory Neurons
attempts.entry_title: Ultrasound responses in the cortico-thalamo-cortical pathway (Gao et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on dandiset 000946, which holds sorted spike times from S1, POm, auditory cortex and M1 of anesthetized rats during transcranial focused ultrasound at several pulse repetition frequencies and duty cycles. The files hold no spike waveforms and no cell types, so only the auditory cortex responses of Figure 11B, which the paper does not split by type, can be tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2025) from dandiset 000946

outcomes.statement: In the 3000 Hz PRF (60% DC) sessions 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs were recorded from S1 and 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs from POm; in the 30 Hz PRF (0.6% DC) sessions 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs from S1 and 189 RSUs and 43 FSUs from POm.
outcomes.source: Figure 4 legend
outcomes.quote: There are 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs recorded from S1, 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 3,000 Hz. There are 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs recorded from S1 and189 RSUs and 43 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 30 Hz.
outcomes.notes: The paper types units as RSUs or FSUs by k-means on the initial phase and afterhyperpolarization of the spike waveform (Methods, Neuronal type classification); no file holds waveforms, and celltype_label is 0 in all 1516 files that have it, so the RSU/FSU split cannot be made. The k-means of the claims file header puts every unit in one of its two clusters, so RSU + FSU is the number of units with more than 2000 spikes under every typing reading, and an area total more than 10% from the paper's RSU + FSU rules out both the reproduced outcome (every count within 10%) and the partial one (area totals within 10%), whatever the split. Units with more than 2000 spikes in distinct recordings with tFUS at S1 and PD 200 us. POm has 352 units at 3000 Hz (339 without the BH499 POM_S1BF recording) against 250, and 315 at 30 Hz against 232, ratios 1.36 to 1.41, so the POm totals are outside 10% under both POm selections. S1 has, at 3000 Hz, 572 over all S1 recordings, 383 in the rats with POm recordings and 234 in the sessions with a POm file (509, 320 and 234 without the suffixed recordings NEAR, NEW and 2; 591 with the S1_R and S1BF files) against 366; at 30 Hz 530, 390 and 213 (624 with S1_R) against 209. One S1 selection matches at 3000 Hz and another at 30 Hz, but none matches both, and POm matches in neither. The POm units come from all 10 POm rats (6 to 65 each at 3000 Hz). The totals depend on which rats and which unit rule are used, though nothing marks a rat for exclusion and the criterion fixes the rule at more than 2000 spikes. Leaving out two of the 10 POm rats brings all three POm totals within 10% for 9 of the 45 pairs (BH511 and BH513 give 227, 241 and 1052). With more than 8000 spikes the POm totals are 242, 230 and 1031, all within 10%, while no S1 selection fits all three at 1000, 2000, 4000 or 8000 spikes; for AC, more than 4000 spikes gives 445 units, inside 453 +/- 45.3. So the paper's unit rule or spike counting may differ from more than 2000 spikes over the whole file. The RSU/FSU split was not tested.
deviations: The RSU/FSU split cannot be made (no waveforms or cell types), so the claim is judged on the area totals, which are the same under every typing reading of the claims file header.

Which sessions count beyond the sessions of the S1 and POm rats is not fixed; every selection the identifiers allow is shown, and the outcome is the same under all of them because the POm totals are outside 10% under each.
Recordings deposited twice (identical spike times and trial starts) are counted once.

The seventh AC rat, BH532, has no PD 200 us recording, and the AC_1 and AC_2 files of BH538 are at 1500 Hz and PD 40 us. The four readings of the claims file header give different outcomes, and the header blocks a claim when they do. N1 with B1 is partially reproduced: Kruskal-Wallis p = 7.83e-06 (0 to 67 ms) and 5.16e-49 (201 to 268 ms); during sonication 1500 Hz (140.3 +/- 8.8%, corrected p = 2.46e-08), 3000 Hz (107.1 +/- 1.2%, 9.72e-11) and also 4500 Hz (108.0 +/- 1.5%, 7.05e-05) are above baseline and 30 Hz is not (105.9%, 0.0189); postsonication exactly 30, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz are above baseline (176.4, 147.9, 310.5 and 210.8%) and 300 Hz is not (94.3%); 300 Hz has the lowest mean in both windows. N1 with B2 is not reproduced: 300 Hz is also above baseline during sonication (99.7%, corrected p = 6.29e-03). N2 with B1 and with B2 are not reproduced (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0213 during sonication). No reading is better supported: N2 gives 49.8 to 61.7% at trial starts shifted by 1 s, where N1 gives 94.3 to 99.0%; under N1 the B1 sample is 100% for every unit, so the two-sample test becomes a test against a constant; B2 uses a window the paper never names. No reading reproduces the claim. With one rat left out, N1 with B1 gives reproduced (without BH537), partially reproduced (without BH530, BH535 or BH538) or not reproduced (without BH539 or BH547, where 30 Hz joins the during set), and N1 with B2 gives reproduced without BH530, BH537 or BH538; 300 Hz has the lowest mean in both windows in all twelve runs. The statement's PRF dependence (both Kruskal-Wallis tests) holds under N1. The question of which normalization and baseline sample the paper used is for the paper's authors (finding methods_unavailable); whether the header's readings N2 and B1 are readings of the paper is asked of a reader (questions/000946.yaml).
deviations: The normalization (N1 or N2) and the baseline sample of the post hoc test (B1 or B2) are not fixed by the paper (Statistical analysis, "normalized to the pre-stim period (67 ms pre-stim)"); all four readings were run and they give different outcomes.
The Bonferroni factor is the five PRF levels of the panel (claims file header, reading C1); reading C2 applies only to a panel with a single comparison.

The dataset holds AC recordings at PD 200 us from 6 rats (7 AC rats in all) where the paper reports 12 S1-AC rats, and it gives 633 units with more than 2000 spikes where the paper reports 453; the paper's selection of AC units could not be matched.

Each PRF comes from 3 or 4 of the 6 rats, and the rats differ by PRF, so the Kruskal-Wallis test across PRFs mixes PRF with rat (for example BH538 averages 654.1% at 3000 Hz, 201 to 268 ms, against 310.5% pooled); the paper also pools units across rats.
Recordings deposited twice (identical spike times and trial starts) are counted once.
Trial start_time is taken as sonication onset; the clock check shows the firing changes after it and not 1 s later, which is consistent with this but does not prove there is no fixed delay.

findings.statement: The spike waveforms are not in the dataset, and the RSU/FSU cell types are not either: no file has waveforms or mean waveforms, and acquisition, analysis and processing are empty in all 1550 unit files. The paper types every S1 and POm unit from its waveform (Methods, Neuronal type classification), so 30 of the 33 claims (all those on RSU or FSU responses or their correlations) cannot be tested, and the RSU/FSU split of the two count claims cannot be tested either.
The units column celltype_label is described as label 1 = RSU, label 2 = FSU, but it is 0 for every unit in the 1516 unit files that have it; 34 unit files have no such column.

734 of the 1550 unit files are second (or third) copies of another file, with identical spike times and trial starts and the same identifier, under session start times up to 57 s apart and different file names; 816 distinct recordings remain. Counting the files as they are would double most unit counts.

No recording is marked as sham (no tFUS) or as tFUS aimed at CG1, the control conditions of Figure 5; every recording gives a PRF and a PD and a target of S1, M1 or POm. If the sham and CG1 sessions are in the dataset, they cannot be found.
The dataset has 10 rats with POm recordings and 7 with AC recordings, where the paper reports 16 S1-POm rats and 12 S1-AC rats (Methods); 20 rats in all.

The AC recordings at PD 200 us give 633 units with more than 2000 spikes (112, 89, 138, 167 and 127 at 30 to 4500 Hz), where Figure 11 reports 453 (83, about 59, 107, 104 and 100), although the dataset has fewer AC rats than the paper. The POm totals exceed the paper's RSU + FSU counts by 36 to 44% under every selection of recordings by identifier (at 3000 Hz 352 against 250, at 30 Hz 315 against 232, over the five PRFs 1470 against 1019), with 10 POm rats where the paper reports 16. They come within 10% only if two of the POm rats are left out (9 of the 45 pairs, for example BH511 and BH513, which nothing marks for exclusion) or if only units with more than 8000 spikes are counted. The paper's unit selection cannot be repeated from its description.

The dataset also holds recordings of M1 and sessions with tFUS aimed at M1 (152 distinct recordings) or at POm (65), and a few recordings labelled S1BF (3), VPM (1), S1_R, S1_1, M1_R (1 each) and AC_1, AC_2 (1 each), none of which the paper describes; the dandiset description mentions only S1, POm and AC with tFUS at S1.

In the 60 sessions at PD 200 us with tFUS at S1 that have files from two of S1, POm and AC (the only sessions checked), both files have identical trial start times, so the areas were recorded together, but their session_start_time values differ (median 15.5 min, up to 3964 min); session_start_time does not give the start of the recording.

The recorded area and the tFUS target are given only in free text in general/notes, in two spellings; the electrodes table has location unknown and the electrode group location is 'brain area'. Five recordings of BH500 leave the area empty, and no other recording does. general/data_collection, which carries the PRF and PD, is empty in 33 recordings (BH494 25, BH499 6, BH500 2), where the identifier gives them; where both are given (782 recordings) they agree.

The arrays of the STTC files do not have the shape their descriptions give: the descriptions list a dimension for nine dt values, while the arrays have the 10 time windows, the trials and the units of the two areas (for example STTC is 10 x 499 x 20 x 9) and no dt dimension. Which dt was used, and which units the rows and columns are, is not stated.

Question for the paper's authors: was the normalized spiking rate the ratio of a unit's mean rate in the window to its mean rate in the 67 ms before stimulation (over trials), or a per-trial ratio averaged over trials; and in the post hoc Wilcoxon test against baseline, what was the baseline sample (the normalized pre-stimulus rates, which are 100% under the first reading, or another pre-stimulus window)? The Statistical analysis says only that rates were normalized to the 67 ms before stimulation. For Figure 11B the readings give different outcomes, and the claim is blocked.

disagreements.reason: The notebook calls this blocked, but its own totals in cell 17 decide it. POm units at 3000 Hz are 352 against 233+17 = 250, and at 30 Hz 315 against 232. Both are far outside 10%, so neither the reproduced outcome (eight counts in tolerance) nor the partial one (area totals within 10%) can be reached under any RSU/FSU split. This is subject to the session selection (item 6): identifiers with suffixes may be repeat or off-target placements the paper left out.

Cell 17 again. S1 totals are 986, 1726 or 2414 depending on the S1 selection, against 1297 +/-10% (1167 to 1427). POm is 1470 against 1019 +/-10%. No split can rescue either. This is subject to the session selection (item 6).

Cell 24: the four method readings give different outcomes. N1/B1 is partial (during-sonication set {1500, 3000, 4500}, one PRF too many). N1/B2 is not reproduced (300 Hz also above baseline during sonication). N2/B1 and N2/B2 are not reproduced (Kruskal-Wallis in 0-67 ms p = 0.0213). The claims header says that when readings differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown. The notebook's judge gives a verdict per reading but never combines them under that rule. No reading reproduces the claim. The unit count is 633 against 453 +/-45.3, outside tolerance. N2 is not a reasonable reading of normalized to the pre-stim period (biased low, 50-62% at shifted onsets), but dropping it would not change fig11b, because N1/B1 and N1/B2 still disagree. Under N1 the B1 baseline sample is exactly 100 for every unit, so the rank-sum test is effectively a one-sample location test. Each PRF comes from only 3 or 4 of 6 rats, so the Kruskal-Wallis across PRFs confounds PRF with rat.

entries.name: 000946-gao-2025
entries.title: Ultrasound responses in the cortico-thalamo-cortical pathway (Gao et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on dandiset 000946, which holds sorted spike times from S1, POm, auditory cortex and M1 of anesthetized rats during transcranial focused ultrasound at several pulse repetition frequencies and duty cycles. The files hold no spike waveforms and no cell types, so only the auditory cortex responses of Figure 11B, which the paper does not split by type, can be tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2025) from dandiset 000946
